statement.title: Second-difference equations for phases
statement.full_tex:
Let $f:\F_2^3\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, let $T$ be a symmetric binary $3\times3$ matrix, and let $\Theta$ be as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:m-M-1}. Then:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
T&\text{equations}&\text{consequence}\\\hline
\operatorname{rank}T=3&\Delta_k\Delta_af=0\ (k\cdot Ta=0)&4\Delta_jf=0\ (j=1,2,3)\\
\operatorname{rank}T=3\text{ or }\operatorname{im}T=\Span\{e_1,e_2\},\ T\ne\Theta&\Delta_{\Theta Ta}\Delta_af=0\ (\text{all }a)&4\Delta_jf=0\ (j=1,2)\\
T=\Theta&\Delta_{\Theta Ta}\Delta_af=0\ (\text{all }a)&2\Delta_jf=0\ (j=1,2)
\end{array}
\]

finite_domain: The 28 nonsingular symmetric binary 3x3 matrices of the first system; the 28 nonsingular and 4 rank-two matrices of the others (60 systems).

covered_subclaims: For each system and each of its target rows, membership in the integer lattice spanned by the rows of the equations.

remaining_work: No verifier of supplied evidence separate from the recomputation.

checker_conventions: paper/conventions.json; each checker states its coordinate order in its docstring
